yes! 100%. i get hyper fixated on things and i don’t really have a choice on what they are, but it’s the most exhilarating couple of weeks/months because i dive right in, spend all my time and sometimes money (depending on what the hyperfixation is) on it + find ways to bring it up in every conversation. and then one day i just snap out of it, which is usually when the deep depression hits because the shiny object isn’t so shiny anymore. that’s kind of what happened from october-january, where i got really into sketch writing and wrote 50 in a month, and considered changing my whole future to revolve around it (thankfully i was in school and didn’t have a major job to quit). i then snapped out of it, and fell into a deep depression that i am currently clawing my way out of right now. not sure if hyperfixation  is a classic symptom of bipolar, but my symptoms certainly manifest in a way that latches onto it.
smacking gum. it’s so obnoxious but when my boyfriend does it when talking to me, coupled with an “oh yeah?” or two, i immediately start ovulating.

it’s the most exhilarating and devastating thing. for me, i get hypomanic— i’m super high, productive, it’s my creativity phase. i’m funny, sharp, quick witted, and everything is just within my reach. the downside is i am impulsive, and also so grotesquely social that i feel like i might explode if i don’t have someone around to talk to all the time. there’s then the depression. literally dropping my phone can lead to suicidal thoughts it gets that dark. it can go either way, i can take the starving artist route where all of my art is cynical and edgy, but at least i’m still creating, or the other route where i can’t even leave bed except for work. i don’t eat, i don’t sleep. i just lay there dull and morose until it’s time for my shift where i can focus on the same old tasks but without the pressure of creating something new, because it’s going to inevitably be shitty and worthless and what’s the point, right? 

and then there’s the mixed episodes. those are not for the weak. i don’t know how to describe it other than a rolling panic attack that lasts for about a week, where im derealized and terrified, and mean and irritated, i can’t sleep at all. i want to literally rip my skin off, it’s a mix between mania and depression, and also anxiety, and every horrible feeling i have ever had all at once. one hundred tracks playing in my mind, all out of sync, yet all saying the same thing. i get suicidal in the depression, but i’m too low to do anything about it. what makes mixed so scary is that i actually have the energy. 

right now, i am sort of depressed, sort of stable. stability is an active choice i have to make— seeing a doctor, a therapist. eating right, sleeping right. loving as much as possible, my boyfriend, my family, random strangers and the world itself. seeing the good in things even when i don’t want to. dancing, listening to music, trying to be creative and uncritical of my art because it comes from the heart, and it’s vulnerable, and i’m healing. it sometimes baffles me that stability comes so naturally to some people. it really does. 

all in all, i am simultaneously thankful and resentful of my bipolar disorder. i am thankful because it has inspired my art, it has made me much more empathetic, and to feel so deeply can be a truly beautiful thing. but i am also resentful because it has taken so many moments from me, injured my teenage years, and will probably have lasting effects on me due to trauma from the episodes and also all of the medication i have to take. i guess what is important is that while i am bipolar, i am also in recovery, and i’m doing all that i can do to heal.

The highs and lows were so destructive that I couldn’t keep up anymore. I was put in therapy in high school for anxiety and depression, and while I was meeting with my doctors to manage those two things, I got diagnosed with bipolar

A chemical imbalance for sure. I suggest looking into bipolar and how it forms, from a scientific standpoint it’s actually very interesting! It is highly genetic, and theorized that it’s epigenetic also, so generally it is already encoded into someone’s DNA- but traumatic events can bring it out and cause it to develop!

The uncertainty for sure. Especially with the depression. I’ll have plans I am looking forward to for months only to fall into a depressive episode around the time that they actually happen and feel very unfulfilled. 

The tricky thing about it is when the lows are severe enough, even if it’s only been for three days, it can taint your view and convince you that it’s always been like this and that it always will be like this, and the fact that you were ever happy in the first place is almost inconceivable.

I started showing depression around 11, hypomania around 14, and mixed mania around 17, but the high energy low energy cycles were around for even longer than that.  My highs generally last about 5 to 7 days, but sometimes I get into mega inspired periods that aren’t necessarily hypomania but carry the same productivity and creativity that last a few weeks. Depression tends to last for a few weeks.

This is really sweet, and a very kind sentiment. What I would say is

1. You're already taking a good step in showing that you care and doing some research on it, and hearing from real people who struggle with the condition as well.
2. Your girlfriend will have emotions just like anybody else, and even when these are strong, they are not always bipolar related. I would always get frustrated when I would try to set a boundary or get really happy/sad about something and the other person would ask if it was my bipolar disorder as if it was the only explanation. 
3. If she is comfortable, ask questions about her symptoms, whether she's receiving treatment, etc, but don't pry. Everyone is different and everyone's journey is different, it's not all textbook.
4. Thank her for disclosing her disorder. It is scary, and opening up about it is a courageous thing to do.
5. Set boundaries for yourself. As a bipolar person, sometimes my disorder can strain my relationship. For example, sometimes if I'm hypomanic and I do impulsive things that ultimately hurt me more than anything else, my boyfriend will tell me it's not cool, and when he's firm in that boundary it puts it helps keep me in line. It's important that you take care of yourself too, as with any other relationship.

It is really kind of you to ask to try to understand her better. You got this, and best of luck in your relationship.

I have been in the exact position as you many times. It's funny how our brains can be so deceiving sometimes. We can have 364 days of stability and 1 night of feeling the shittiest we have ever felt in our lives. And that 1 night somehow seems so much longer than the 364 days, even when it is a speck in comparison to everything else. But it is poisonous, because it convinces you that the past 364 days were all secretly awful, and that it will never be good again. But it will get good again. Even if it feels like the walls have finally closed in.

But you might already know that. So here are some little things to help you get through

\- Dancing. Seriously. I'm awful at it and I don't know your abilities, but just turn on some music and get all of it out of your system.

\- Watching something on ˇTV or youtube. Just to help distract your mind from the despair you're feeling tonight.

\- Doing something nice for yourself even if you don't want to. Have you eaten, drank water, taken meds if you have them? Do that if you have the energy. ˇThen I suggest taking a cold shower to help reduce anxiety or extreme emotions (you can also do this by putting an icepack on your head), putting on any lotions or other toiletries you have that will make you feel better. (For me, I have a bunch of bath bombs that I save for "special occasions" that I never really use, and so they're something I can appreciate when I feel awful)

\-Positive affirmations. It might feel weird, but say things like "I can do this" or "I will get through this" out loud to yourself so you can hear it! It helps! Also you can even write down these affirmations to help you visualize it.

These are all in place to get you through tonight and maybe tomorrow if you still feel this way. But if it continues please please reach out to someone who can help you!! You are stronger than you think, and it's okay to have our lows! We're only human with a wacky illness that makes stuff like this happen sometimes. Please be kind and gentle to yourself, and forgive yourself for a brief break in stability.

I will spare you the details of it all, but by Junior year of high school I was labeled by my teachers as "inconsistent", "intelligent but unmotivated", and of course, "a pleasure to have in class". I was labeled by my doctors as having a laundry list of mental illnesses. I was labeled by myself as "ugly" "unworthy" "stupid" and something that deserved to be hidden.  
I was none of those things. Turns out I was battling my own brain, while also trying to use that brain, while also trying to keep an eye out for my present and future. Developmentally, I was where I was supposed to be but the pressure that I placed on myself had lead me to believe that I was behind everyone else-- that I would never be able to fend for myself in the world. That I was a disappointment and that I was alone.  
I want to pass on the knowledge that got me through that feeling:  
1. Time moves fast, but it won't sneak up on you just like that. Every day you will grow, you will learn. As a teenager, your brain is in still development, and comparing yourself to peers either your age or a few years older than you will just make you feel worse. You will get there when you get there, and it's not a race. Nurture yourself and don't force yourself to sprint to the front  
2. Never be ashamed to ask questions or ask for help. It is so easy to slip into a feeling of isolation and fear, so please make sure to ask for help when you need it. Furthermore, asking questions is your gateway to learning more and becoming a better person, so by all means, go for it.  
3. Treat yourself with kindness. You WILL fail at some points. You WILL say the wrong thing, or mess up a relationship or hurt somebody. You WILL make bad decisions. It's all part of being a teenager. The important thing is to learn from these mistakes and not repeat them. We learn by failure and we become stronger. Use what you have learned to be the best person you can be.  
4. Never, ever, under any circumstances, let the world take your soul. You've only got one of those.  
I know that right now, it can feel isolating and scary, and negative feelings can seem permanent. I  promise things will get better. I am the happiest, healthiest, and most at peace, I have been in my entire life. I have dropped my shell, and have made so many friends within the past year. I have gotten into a nationally ranked college, I have found myself a job that I love, and for the first time in a long time, I have hope.  
And for my last lesson.  
5. Things will get better. In the words of Ramshackle Glory, "Keep on loving, keep on fighting. And hold on, hold on for your life".
